QS hardening: observability and lifecycle gaps found during the queue-split run
description: Three issues surfaced while running the QS epic at --concurrency 4 that the queue-split itself does not address. (1) The buffered mirror event sink silently DROPS events when its channel fills (cmd/yolo-agent/main.go newMirrorEventSink: select-default discards), so monitoring undercounts task completions under load - this masked the real progress of every multi-worker run. (2) The agent leaves orphaned codex `app-server` child processes when it dies abnormally. (3) The agent emits no run_finished event when it dies from a fatal runtime error (e.g. the concurrent-map panic, now fixed in d81504b2), making post-mortems guesswork. The map race itself is already fixed; these are the durability/observability gaps it exposed.

title: QS-HARD-4 Queue-mode run misreported as failed (exit 3) despite task success
description:
Why: The live isolation gate ran one beads task through `run --queue` + a standalone runner. The task fully succeeded — implement+review in an isolated clone, merge+push to origin/main (af199b85), work_results status=completed, beads task closed — but the producer emitted run_finished=failed and exited with status 3. The per-task result mapping is correct (internal/agent/queue_dispatcher.go closes on completed); the misreport is at the producer loop/shutdown level after the task closed.

In scope: find where the queue-mode producer run returns a non-nil error / exit 3 after a successful --max 1 task (candidates: post-task NextTasks/IsComplete via the beads `br` CLI, queue dispatcher Close, embedded-runner detection). Make a fully-successful queue run report run_finished=completed and exit 0.

Strict TDD: add a failing test asserting a queue-mode run with one completed task returns nil/exit 0; fix; verify.

Done when: a successful queue run exits 0 with run_finished=completed.

Expected files: cmd/yolo-agent/main.go or internal/agent/loop.go + test.
close_reason: Fixed in d72ac2ea: br close is now idempotent; queue run exits 0 after a completed task. Root cause was double-close (loop + dispatcher) on an already-closed task returning exit 3.

title: QS-HARD-5 Standalone runner does not emit runner_output to its event stream

Why: During the gate, the standalone runner's per-process event file (~/.yolo-runner/events/<runner-id>.jsonl) received only a single runner_started event for the whole implement run — no runner_output/heartbeat/progress — so `events follow | yolo-tui` was blank while codex worked. The executor streams progress via OnProgress, but it does not reach the runner daemon's per-item event sink.

In scope: wire the executor's progress events through to the runner daemon's event sink so runner_output/heartbeat/review/landing events are written to the per-process event file.

Strict TDD: fake executor emits progress; assert the runner's event sink receives runner_output. 

Done when: a runner implement run writes its progress stream to ~/.yolo-runner/events/<id>.jsonl.

Expected files: cmd/yolo-agent/runner_implement.go / runner_daemon.go + test.

title: PR review v2: cross-project discovery, per-PR checkout, project auto-detection
description: Redesign the PR-review path to beat the in-tree competitor (taxi/tplatform/ai_infra/ai_minion/pr_review_poller). That competitor polls `arc pr list` and runs Claude via the Arcanum MCP against a SHARED trunk mount, reading diffs only - it never checks out the PR. Ours must be execution-grade: discover PRs assigned to genaevstratov via `arc pr list --json -i --status open` (cross-Arcadia, drop the configured-workspaces model); materialize a FRESH isolated arc checkout per PR (arc init --object-store <shared> <per-pr-mount> + arc pr checkout <id> --detached) so the agent works inside the real PR code and may build/run tests; auto-detect the project (changed paths -> nearest ya.make root; read CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; build cmd `ya make -t <proj>`; fetch linked Startrek tickets from pr.issues for AC). Keep the built-in arc CLI + Arcanum HTTP API (no MCP). Reuse the existing arcreview review cycle, prompt builder, and reply/review/ship appliers + arcanum API clients; the writeback path (internal/sources/arcpr/writeback.go) is unchanged. This corrects the earlier kind-aware isolation choice that gave pr-review a shared-mount read view. Shipping stays OFF (allow_ship:false) until a full cycle is watched. Read the approved plan before every task.

title: Hot config reload for long-running yolo-agent watchers
description: Long-running watchers should pick up .yolo-runner/config.yaml edits without a restart. Today tracker-watch resolves trackerAgentConfig once at startup (cmd/yolo-agent/tracker_watch.go:38) and threads that stale value through every poll iteration, and both tracker-watch and arc-review-watch capture poll_interval at startup. arc-review-watch already re-resolves its config every iteration (arc_review_watch.go:114) but nothing pins that behavior. This epic makes per-iteration config resolution the rule: labels, status transitions, agent defaults, and poll intervals apply on the next poll after a config edit. Deliberately startup-bound and out of scope: lock_path (the held lock is never re-acquired), state_path, events path/stream wiring, and profile/tracker endpoint identity.

Observed in production three times in two days: a Startrek HTTP 500 on issues/_search (adapta-watch-20260610_154329, died 03:32 after ~12h of correct operation), a stale scheduler-state 'task not found' (since fixed), and a non-idempotent status transition (since fixed). The watcher should log/emit the error, keep polling, and only exit on context cancellation or a bounded run of consecutive failures. The Startrek client should additionally retry transient 5xx responses on idempotent requests.

Sequencing note: the HCR epic (yolo-8des) also modifies runTrackerWatchPollLoop's signature (interval provider). Do not run both epics' loop tasks concurrently; land one before starting the other.
